I dashed, they told me Sen was in an accident last night. This was no time to worry about the competition. With Sen being the only thought, I dashed my way to the hospital, rushing past the reception, looking out with the corner of my eyes. It was a small village hospital, and among one of those corridors, I saw, Sen’s family. Making my way to them, I saw how his mother stood up, in tears at my sight, almost about to break up again, when I took her hands, “Aunty, don’t worry, ….” Before I could say anything more, she told me how the doctors said it was a severe head trauma, and how her child might never wake up again. “He has duked it out so many times aunty, his head is stronger than you think, I am sure he will wake up soon laughing his injury off.” Telling her, and myself at the same time. But her expressions suddenly changed. “It’s Sachiko whose inside…not Sen.” Then where is Sen, was what my face must have said cause even when I stayed silent in shock of this unexpected development, the boy sitting behind spoke, he was just here a while ago. It was not appropriate but I dashed, not knowing where to head, but knowing he must be, yeah, on the roof and that’s where I headed to.

The roof was all filled with white sheets hung up to dry. Slowly making my ways through them, to the other end, I finally saw, a figure, that I could make out of, from even under the sheets. I went and took off the sheet that covered his body while he was laying on a bench. His face calm, and the Rosario in his hands gripped tightly, I could see him, yes I could. “Where have I seen this angel somewhere before too” he said, lifting his hand to me, “hey Mr. Angel, would you please make it so, that it’s me who you take to heavens and not Sachiko.” It reminded me of the first time I ever met him, and later in the future, it would come to remind me, how it was the last time I met him as well.
